questions.q: Which component receives every request in Spring MVC and delegates it?
o: `DispatcherServlet`
`RequestMapping`
`ViewResolver`
`BeanFactory`
questions.w: It is the front controller. It uses handler mappings to find the controller and adapters to call it.

questions.q: What is the difference between `@Controller` and `@RestController`?
o: `@RestController` adds `@ResponseBody`, so results are written as the body
`@RestController` is able to return only plain strings
`@Controller` is not able to map any URLs at all
The two annotations are completely identical in behaviour
questions.w: With `@Controller` a returned String is treated as a view name. With `@RestController` it is serialised, usually as JSON.

questions.q: How do you read a value from the URL path `/accounts/42`?
o: `@PathVariable`, with `@GetMapping("/accounts/{id}")`
`@RequestParam` with the id after a comma
`@RequestBody` on a string parameter
`@ModelAttribute` with no mapping
questions.w: `@RequestParam` reads query strings (`?id=42`). `@RequestBody` reads and deserialises the request body.

questions.q: What does `@Valid` on a `@RequestBody` parameter trigger?
o: Bean Validation, and an exception when a constraint fails
Encryption of the whole request body before it is read
A uniqueness check against the database for each field
Caching of the response so repeat calls are quicker
questions.w: Handle the exception globally and return a `400` with field errors. Use annotations such as `@NotBlank` and `@Positive` on the DTO.

questions.q: What is the best place to translate exceptions into consistent HTTP error responses?
o: A `@RestControllerAdvice` with `@ExceptionHandler` methods
A `try/catch` block inside every controller method
The database access layer, next to the repositories
The front-end code, after the response has been received
questions.w: Central handling keeps controllers clean and error bodies uniform, for example using `ProblemDetail`.

questions.q: What is the role of a `HandlerInterceptor`?
o: Runs code before and after a controller, for concerns like logging
Parses the JSON request body into a Java object
Creates the database connections for each request
Defines the scopes that beans in the context may have
questions.w: Servlet filters run earlier and see raw requests. Interceptors know the matched handler and run inside the DispatcherServlet.

questions.q: Which library usually converts Java objects to JSON in Spring MVC?
o: Jackson, through `HttpMessageConverter`s
Hibernate, through its entity mappings
Thymeleaf, through its template engine
Tomcat, through its connector threads
questions.w: Content negotiation uses the `Accept` header to choose a converter. Customise Jackson with `ObjectMapper` settings or annotations.

o: Business rules belong in services, which can be tested without HTTP
Controllers are not allowed to call services
Thin controllers run faster in Tomcat
Spring forbids any logic in controllers
questions.w: A controller should translate HTTP to a service call and the result back to HTTP, nothing more.
